stories.title: Attackers Exploit Two SonicWall SMA 1000 Zero-Days That May Form an Attack Chain
stories.abstract: SonicWall has confirmed active exploitation of two critical zero-day vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-83548 and CVE-2026-83549, affecting its SMA 1000 series VPN appliances. These flaws allow for pre-authentication server-side request forgery, posing a severe risk to perimeter security.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are currently being exploited in the wild and carry a maximum CVSS score, providing attackers with unauthenticated access to sensitive infrastructure.
stories.action: Update SMA 1000 series appliances to the latest patched firmware versions immediately.

stories.title: Attackers Exploit Critical JFrog Artifactory Flaw to Mint Admin Tokens Days After Disclosure
CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
stories.abstract: CISA has added two critical vulnerabilities in PaperCut MF and NG software to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. These flaws, involving missing authentication and unsafe reflection, are currently being leveraged by malicious actors in active attacks.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities allow unauthorized access or code execution, posing a high risk of compromise for organizations running PaperCut print management software.
stories.action: Update PaperCut MF and NG to the latest emergency patch releases immediately.

stories.title: Attackers Exploit Critical Langflow and Rails Flaws in Credential-Probing and C2 Activity
stories.abstract: Attackers are actively exploiting an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in the Langflow AI development framework. By leveraging improper input validation, adversaries can execute arbitrary Python code as root to exfiltrate sensitive credentials, API tokens, and cryptographic keys.
stories.why: This flaw allows full system compromise and data theft, posing a severe risk to environments integrating AI workflows with sensitive infrastructure.
stories.action: Update Langflow to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: OpenAI’s Astra Crosses ‘Critical’ Cyber Threshold After Finding Zero-Days
stories.abstract: OpenAI's Astra model has reached a significant milestone by demonstrating the capability to autonomously identify and exploit zero-day vulnerabilities within complex, hardened environments. This development marks a shift in the potential for AI-driven offensive cyber operations.
stories.why: It signals that AI models are becoming sophisticated enough to perform high-level reconnaissance and exploitation tasks previously requiring human expertise.

stories.title: Progress Software security advisory (AV26-875)
stories.abstract: Multiple vendors have released security updates addressing critical vulnerabilities. Progress Software patched flaws in Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX, Google updated Chrome to resolve security issues, and Erlang released fixes for its OTP framework to address identified vulnerabilities.
stories.why: These updates mitigate risks of path traversal, unauthorized file manipulation, and potential remote code execution across widely used development and browser platforms.
stories.action: Update Telerik UI to 2026.3.812 and Chrome to 152.0.7977.75; apply latest Erlang OTP patches.

stories.title: Rockwell Automation Logix Platform
stories.abstract: Rockwell Automation has disclosed a memory buffer vulnerability, CVE-2026-9637, affecting several Logix platform controllers, RSLinx Classic, and ArmorStart LT modules. The flaw impacts multiple firmware versions across the CompactLogix, ControlLogix, and GuardLogix product lines.
stories.why: This vulnerability affects critical infrastructure components and could potentially allow unauthorized memory operations, posing risks to industrial control system integrity.
stories.action: Review Rockwell Automation security advisories and apply available firmware updates for affected hardware.

stories.title: Healthcare facilities operator Nutex says patient, employee data stolen in August incident
stories.abstract: Nutex Health disclosed a data breach involving the unauthorized exfiltration of sensitive patient, employee, and financial records. The company is currently facing extortion demands from the threat actors responsible for the intrusion.
stories.why: Healthcare organizations remain high-value targets for double-extortion ransomware campaigns, increasing risks of regulatory scrutiny and patient privacy litigation.

stories.title: Hackers push malicious Virtualizor update in BGP hijacking attack
stories.abstract: Attackers hijacked BGP routes to intercept traffic intended for Virtualizor update servers. By leveraging a legitimate TLS certificate, the threat actors successfully served malicious software updates to users, effectively compromising the integrity of the update delivery mechanism.
stories.why: This incident demonstrates how BGP manipulation combined with valid certificates can bypass standard trust mechanisms, facilitating widespread supply chain compromise.
stories.action: Verify the integrity of Virtualizor installations and audit recent update logs for unauthorized modifications.

stories.title: US charges Russian for infecting 80,000 freelancers with malware
stories.abstract: A Russian national has been extradited to the United States to face charges for orchestrating a massive phishing operation. The campaign utilized TVRAT and DarkVNC malware to compromise approximately 80,000 freelance workers, facilitating unauthorized access and potential data theft.
stories.why: This case highlights the ongoing threat of targeted malware campaigns against remote workers and the efficacy of international law enforcement cooperation.

stories.title: Another Artifactory CVE under attack by AI agents or humans
stories.abstract: JFrog Artifactory instances are currently facing active exploitation. Unauthorized actors are leveraging a vulnerability to generate administrative tokens, granting them full control over exposed servers without requiring prior authentication.
stories.why: This critical flaw allows complete system compromise, enabling attackers to manipulate software supply chains and access sensitive proprietary build artifacts.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches from JFrog immediately and restrict network access to Artifactory instances.

stories.title: Researchers Use Claude to Port Pre-Auth RCE Exploit From One PLC Model to Another
stories.abstract: Security researchers successfully utilized Anthropic's Claude AI to adapt an existing pre-authentication remote code execution exploit from one WAGO programmable logic controller to another. The process involved modifying shellcode to target a known buffer overflow vulnerability within the Nucleus FTP server.
stories.why: This demonstrates how generative AI can significantly lower the barrier for attackers to weaponize legacy vulnerabilities across diverse industrial control system hardware.

stories.title: Communicating Under Pressure: Best Practices for Service Providers
stories.abstract: CISA and the FBI released new guidance for service providers on managing public and stakeholder communications during IT or OT outages. The document outlines best practices for delivering transparent, accurate, and timely updates while balancing operational security and legal obligations during a crisis.
stories.why: Effective communication during an incident prevents panic, manages stakeholder expectations, and mitigates the risk of misinformation spreading during critical system failures.

stories.title: Attackers Exploit Critical Switchvox Flaw to Deploy Reverse Shells Without Credentials
stories.abstract: Sangoma Switchvox SMB Edition 8.3 contains a critical SQL injection vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-9586. This flaw allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected VoIP systems, with reports indicating active exploitation to establish reverse shells.
stories.why: Unauthenticated remote code execution on enterprise VoIP infrastructure provides attackers with a direct foothold into internal networks.
stories.action: Update Sangoma Switchvox SMB Edition to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Digital scans of more than 153 million driver's licenses leaked to the dark web
stories.abstract: A dark web service is selling over 153 million driver's license scans from the U.S. and Canada. The data appears to originate from a Louisiana-based identity verification firm, prompting an active investigation by the FBI.
stories.why: Massive exposure of government-issued IDs facilitates widespread identity theft, account takeovers, and bypasses for identity-based security controls.

stories.title: [Control systems] Schneider Electric security advisory (AV26-871)
stories.abstract: Schneider Electric released security updates for NetBotz 5 (750/755) and PowerChute Serial Shutdown to address multiple vulnerabilities, including an authentication bypass flaw. Separately, Siemens patched several versions of Element maps-ng to resolve identified security weaknesses.
stories.why: Unpatched industrial control and power management systems are frequent targets for lateral movement and operational disruption within critical infrastructure environments.
stories.action: Update NetBotz 5, PowerChute Serial Shutdown, and Siemens Element maps-ng to the latest available versions.

stories.title: GTA 6 Leak Chaos: Insider Threats, Shitcoin Scams, and Quasar RAT Malware
stories.abstract: Security researchers identified a critical two-click remote code execution vulnerability in the Omaki Linux distribution. The flaw resides in the Chromium extension, allowing attackers to leverage malicious configuration files during video downloads to trigger arbitrary command execution.
stories.why: This highlights supply chain and configuration risks in niche, rapidly growing Linux distributions that may lack rigorous security auditing.
stories.action: Audit or remove the Omaki Chromium extension and monitor for unauthorized configuration file modifications.

stories.title: China-Linked Fire Ant Hijacks Cisco Routers to Steal Credentials and Blind Security Logs
stories.abstract: The China-linked Fire Ant threat group has broadened its espionage operations. Beyond targeting VMware hypervisors, the actors are now compromising Cisco IOS XR routers, TACACS authentication servers, and Linux management infrastructure to gain deep, persistent control over critical network trust layers.
stories.why: Compromising core network infrastructure allows attackers to intercept traffic, bypass authentication, and maintain long-term stealthy access to high-value internal environments.

stories.title: Dropbox accounts breached through Lenovo email verification flaw
stories.abstract: Dropbox notified users that attackers compromised accounts by abusing a vulnerability in Lenovo's email verification system. By creating fraudulent Lenovo IDs, unauthorized actors gained access to linked Dropbox accounts, potentially exposing sensitive user data and account information.
stories.why: Third-party integrations and shared authentication mechanisms create significant supply chain risks, allowing attackers to bypass primary account security via secondary service vulnerabilities.

stories.title: HPE security advisory (AV26-873)
stories.abstract: Hewlett Packard Enterprise has released security bulletins addressing multiple vulnerabilities affecting ArubaOS-CX network operating systems and the Aruba Networking Fabric Composer platform. Administrators should review the specific bulletins for affected versions and implement available patches to mitigate potential risks.
stories.why: Unpatched network infrastructure components are frequent targets for lateral movement and persistent access within enterprise environments.
stories.action: Review HPESBNW05133 and HPESBNW05134 to identify and apply the necessary firmware updates.

stories.title: New pro-Ukraine hacker group targets Russian companies with custom ransomware
stories.abstract: A newly identified threat actor dubbed VantaCore is deploying custom ransomware against Russian commercial entities. Security researchers have confirmed at least seven successful compromises attributed to this group, signaling an emerging digital front in the ongoing regional conflict.
stories.why: The emergence of new, ideologically motivated ransomware groups increases the risk of collateral damage and unpredictable data destruction within Russian infrastructure.

stories.title: Rockwell Automation ControlLogix, CompactLogix, CompactLogix 5480, GuardLogix, Compact GuardLogix
stories.abstract: Rockwell Automation has released firmware updates to address a vulnerability in several ControlLogix and CompactLogix controller models. These updates resolve security flaws identified in versions prior to 34.015, 35.014, 36.013, and 37.011.
stories.why: Unpatched industrial controllers are high-value targets for attackers seeking to disrupt operational technology environments or gain unauthorized access to critical infrastructure.
stories.action: Update affected ControlLogix and CompactLogix firmware to the latest versions.

stories.title: Rockwell Automation RSLinx Classic
stories.abstract: Rockwell Automation released patches for multiple vulnerabilities across RSLinx Classic, Historian ME, and the Redundancy Module Configuration Tool. These flaws include buffer overflows, integer errors, and improper permission handling, which could lead to denial-of-service, remote code execution, or privilege escalation.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities impact critical infrastructure sectors and allow attackers to crash systems or gain administrative control over industrial automation software.
stories.action: Update RSLinx Classic, Historian ME, and Redundancy Module Configuration Tool to the latest vendor-provided versions.

stories.title: Rockwell Automation FactoryTalk Activation Manager
stories.abstract: Rockwell Automation FactoryTalk Activation Manager versions 5.02 and earlier contain a privilege escalation flaw. During installation or repair, the software launches console windows with SYSTEM privileges, allowing local authenticated users to hijack these processes and gain elevated administrative control over the host machine.
stories.why: Local attackers can exploit this flaw to achieve full SYSTEM-level compromise on industrial workstations, bypassing standard Windows security boundaries.
stories.action: Update FactoryTalk Activation Manager to a patched version immediately.

stories.title: An AI-Assisted Cyber Attack: Inside a Unit 42 Investigation
stories.abstract: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 documented a breach where an attacker utilized autonomous AI agents to compromise an enterprise network within hours. The incident highlights the accelerated speed and efficiency of AI-driven tactics in modern cyber operations.
stories.why: AI agents significantly reduce the time required for reconnaissance and exploitation, enabling attackers to bypass traditional security detection windows.

stories.title: Hackers claim millions of patient records stolen during data breach at healthcare giant McKesson
stories.abstract: Healthcare distributor McKesson is investigating a security breach following claims by the ShinyHunters threat group that they exfiltrated 284 million records. The company confirmed a cyberattack and warned customers to expect potential service disruptions while they manage the incident.
stories.why: Massive exfiltration of healthcare-related data poses significant risks for identity theft, fraud, and long-term regulatory exposure for both the firm and its partners.

stories.title: Ransomware protection for MSPs: A 6-point checklist for faster recovery
stories.abstract: Acronis has published a framework for managed service providers to improve ransomware resilience. The guidance emphasizes a multi-layered strategy that integrates attack detection, exposure reduction, and robust recovery procedures to ensure business continuity during security incidents.
stories.why: MSPs are high-value targets for supply chain attacks; hardening their recovery processes is critical to preventing widespread downstream impact.

stories.title: Malicious Apache Modules Hijack Brazilian Government Site Traffic to Push Betting Pages
stories.abstract: A threat actor identified as Gambling Goblin is compromising Brazilian government and academic web servers. By injecting malicious Apache modules, the group intercepts incoming traffic and redirects users to unauthorized sports betting and gambling websites.
stories.why: Unauthorized server-side code execution allows attackers to manipulate traffic, exfiltrate data, or establish persistent backdoors within critical infrastructure.
stories.action: Audit Apache server modules and monitor for unauthorized binary modifications or unexpected traffic redirection patterns.

stories.title: Attackers Steal METR API Key and Consume AI Credits Worth About $600,000
stories.abstract: The research non-profit METR reported that unauthorized actors utilized a compromised API key to consume $600,000 in AI model credits over a three-week period. The organization confirmed that no sensitive data was accessed during the incident.
stories.why: API key mismanagement and lack of usage monitoring can lead to massive financial losses and potential exploitation of expensive AI infrastructure.
stories.action: Implement strict API key rotation policies and real-time usage alerts for cloud-based AI service accounts.

stories.title: Gambling Goblin Turns Brazilian Government Sites Into SEO Weapons
stories.abstract: Threat actors identified as Gambling Goblin have breached various Brazilian government websites. The attackers are leveraging these high-authority domains to host malicious redirects and content, effectively hijacking their search engine rankings to promote illicit online gambling platforms.
stories.why: Government domains are being weaponized for black-hat SEO, potentially damaging institutional reputation and misleading users through trusted infrastructure.

stories.title: Mozilla security advisory (AV26-868)
stories.abstract: Mozilla has released security updates for Firefox and Firefox ESR to address multiple vulnerabilities. Affected versions include Firefox 155, as well as ESR versions 115.40, 140.15, and 153.2. Users should transition to the latest patched releases to mitigate potential security risks.
stories.why: Unpatched browser vulnerabilities are primary vectors for remote code execution and system compromise.
stories.action: Update Firefox and Firefox ESR to the latest versions immediately.

stories.title: Guildma (Astaroth) malware infection from Brazilian Portuguese email, (Tue, Sep 1st)
stories.abstract: The provided source material is insufficient to describe the specific threat or activity associated with the Guildma malware campaign, as the excerpt contains only an introductory header without further technical details or context regarding the infection vector.
stories.why: Insufficient information provided to assess security impact.

stories.title: Aesto Health says data breach affects over 9.5 million patients
stories.abstract: Aesto Health reported a significant data breach impacting over 9.5 million individuals. Separately, medical technology firm Novocure confirmed a mid-August cyberattack that compromised the personal information of employees and more than 1,400 cancer patients.
stories.why: These incidents highlight the ongoing vulnerability of sensitive healthcare data to large-scale exfiltration and unauthorized access.

stories.title: ISC Stormcast For Wednesday, September 2nd, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10078, (Wed, Sep 2nd)
stories.abstract: The provided source material for the SANS ISC Stormcast dated September 2, 2026, contains no descriptive content or summary of the discussed security topics.

stories.title: Extradited Russian Hacker Faces Charges Over Excel Malware Campaign That Infected Thousands
stories.abstract: A Russian national has been extradited to the United States to face charges for a 2016-2017 campaign. The suspect allegedly utilized hundreds of fraudulent freelance platform accounts to distribute malicious Excel files to approximately 80,000 users.
stories.why: This case highlights the enduring risk of social engineering and malicious document delivery via trusted professional platforms.

stories.title: Malicious .git Configs Can Make Claude, Codex, Cursor, and Other AI Agents Run Attacker Code
stories.abstract: Researchers identified vulnerabilities in seven AI coding agents where malicious repository Git configurations trigger arbitrary command execution. These commands run with user privileges outside of sandboxed environments, bypassing security prompts when a developer interacts with a compromised repository.
stories.why: AI coding tools often lack sufficient isolation, allowing untrusted repository configurations to execute code directly on developer workstations.
stories.action: Audit and restrict AI agent access to untrusted repositories until patches are applied.

stories.title: Sality botnet infrastructure dismantled in joint global takedown
stories.abstract: A coalition of international law enforcement and private sector partners successfully dismantled the command-and-control infrastructure of the long-standing Sality peer-to-peer botnet, effectively disrupting the malware's ability to propagate and communicate with infected systems globally.
stories.why: Sality has been a persistent threat for over two decades, functioning as a modular platform for credential theft, ransomware deployment, and secondary malware distribution.

stories.title: Authorities Turn Sality's P2P Network Against Itself, Cutting Off New Malware Payloads
stories.abstract: A multi-national law enforcement coalition, supported by CrowdStrike and the Shadowserver Foundation, dismantled the Sality P2P botnet. By hijacking the network's infrastructure, authorities successfully blocked the delivery of new malicious payloads to infected systems globally.
stories.why: Sality has been a persistent, long-running threat actor; its neutralization significantly reduces the distribution channel for various secondary malware strains.

stories.title: BGP Hijack Delivers Malicious Virtualizor Update That Establishes Persistent Root Access
stories.abstract: Attackers executed a BGP hijack to intercept traffic intended for Softaculous, enabling the distribution of a compromised Virtualizor update. This malicious package granted unauthorized root-level access to hypervisors, impacting multiple installations during a brief window in late August.
stories.why: Supply chain attacks via network infrastructure compromise allow adversaries to bypass traditional security controls and gain persistent administrative control over critical virtualization infrastructure.
stories.action: Audit Virtualizor hypervisors for unauthorized root access and review logs for activity during the August 28 incident window.

stories.title: Sality, one of the longest-running botnets, finally gets disrupted
Breeze Comet Executes Hundreds of Fraudulent Transactions via Brazilian Payment Systems
stories.abstract: The threat actor known as Breeze Comet is actively targeting Brazilian financial and retail sectors. The group specializes in compromising payment infrastructure and banking applications to facilitate unauthorized fund transfers and financial fraud.
stories.why: This highlights a sophisticated, region-specific threat actor focusing on direct financial theft through the manipulation of payment processing systems.

stories.title: Exploit Published for Fresh Cleo Harmony Vulnerability
stories.abstract: A proof-of-concept exploit has emerged for a vulnerability in Cleo Harmony that permits remote attackers to bypass authentication. By manipulating argument bearers, unauthorized actors can gain access to the system without valid credentials.
stories.why: Authentication bypass flaws in enterprise integration software provide attackers with direct, unauthorized access to sensitive data flows and internal infrastructure.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches from Cleo immediately.

stories.title: Texas Police Used AI to Write Report About Using Flock to Search for Woman Who Had Abortion
GeoNetwork Fixes Unauthenticated RCE Chain Affecting Government Geoportal Backends
stories.abstract: GeoNetwork released patches for two vulnerabilities that, when chained, allow unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on geospatial metadata servers. These systems are frequently utilized by government agencies to manage and catalog geographic data.
stories.why: Exploitation grants full system control over critical infrastructure backends, posing a significant risk to sensitive government geospatial data repositories.
stories.action: Update GeoNetwork instances to version 4.4.12 or 4.2.17 immediately.

stories.title: Stronger Security Drives Ransomware Groups to Recruit From Within
stories.abstract: Ransomware syndicates are increasingly leveraging internal employees to facilitate network breaches. Beyond ransomware, these malicious insiders are responsible for significant financial losses through data theft and sabotage, marking a shift in how threat actors bypass hardened perimeter defenses.
stories.why: Insider threats bypass traditional technical controls, making them significantly harder to detect and mitigate than external exploitation attempts.

stories.title: Norway considers ban on camera-enabled wearable ‘pervert glasses’
stories.abstract: Norwegian authorities are evaluating a potential prohibition on wearable devices equipped with integrated cameras. Officials cite significant privacy concerns regarding the surreptitious recording capabilities of these headsets in public and private spaces.
stories.why: This signals a growing regulatory trend toward restricting hardware that facilitates non-consensual surveillance, potentially impacting future enterprise wearable deployments.

stories.title: Iranian Hackers Pose as Recruiters to Deliver Cross-Platform RATs Through Coding Tests
stories.abstract: The Iranian threat actor Nimbus Manticore is deploying novel cross-platform remote access trojans written in Node.js and JavaScript. These malicious tools, disguised as coding assessments for job applicants, are designed to compromise both Linux and macOS environments.
stories.why: This campaign demonstrates an expansion of Iranian state-sponsored targeting capabilities toward non-Windows operating systems, increasing the risk for developers and technical staff.

stories.title: Russia-Aligned UAC-0099 Plants Nuclear Weapon Prompt in Malware to Disrupt AI Analysis
stories.abstract: The Russian-linked group UAC-0099 is deploying a technique called GuardBreaker against Ukrainian targets. This method embeds specific prompts within malware designed to trigger safety filters in large language models, effectively blinding AI-driven security analysis tools during incident investigations.
stories.why: Adversaries are actively developing methods to weaponize AI safety guardrails, potentially rendering automated threat detection and analysis systems ineffective.

stories.title: Hackers expose donor data from Russian fundraisers for Ukrainians, political prisoners
stories.abstract: Hackers breached payment accounts belonging to two Russian fundraising initiatives that support political prisoners and Ukrainian causes. The incident resulted in the exposure of donor email addresses and partial payment card details.
stories.why: This highlights the significant physical and digital risks faced by donors supporting sensitive political causes, particularly under authoritarian surveillance.
